Milwaukee County by the numbers

Where do you record a deed in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin?

Deeds and mortgages for Milwaukee County property are recorded at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee, WI 53233. You can bring the paperwork to that room or mail it. The office is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the main number is (414) 278-4021.

The Register of Deeds does more than file deeds. It records, scans and indexes real estate documents, corporation papers and military discharges, records informal probate instruments, keeps financing statements, and collects the real estate transfer fee. Birth, death and marriage certificates come from the same office.

Milwaukee County is the most populous county in Wisconsin, with an estimated 924,216 residents on July 1, 2025 according to the Census Bureau. Every one of those residents lives inside a city or village, because Milwaukee County is the only Wisconsin county with no unincorporated towns. Every address sits in one of 19 municipalities, 10 cities and 9 villages, and one county Register of Deeds records for all of them.

What does it cost to record a document in Milwaukee County?

Recording a standard document costs $30, no matter how many pages it has. Plats, certified copies and the sale transfer fee are charged separately. The office accepts cash, checks and money orders payable to the Register of Deeds. It does not accept credit or debit cards.

ItemAmountSource
Recording fee per document (not a plat)$30Register of Deeds recording page
Certified copy bought at recording$2 first page, $1 each added page, $1 to certifyRegister of Deeds recording page
Subdivision plat recording$50Register of Deeds recording page
Condominium plat$100 review (separate check) plus $50 recordingRegister of Deeds recording page
Department of Transportation plat$25Register of Deeds recording page
Termination of decedent's interest$30Register of Deeds recording page

Any other documents that travel with a plat are charged the standard $30 each. If the deed is a sale, the state transfer fee shows up on your transfer return receipt, and you pay it at the counter together with the recording fee.

How is the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee figured?

The fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction of $100 on a conveyance that is not exempt, which works out to $3 per $1,000. Wisconsin law puts it on the grantor, the seller, and tells the register of deeds to collect it when the deed is submitted. This comes from Wis. Stat. 77.22. On a $200,000 sale the fee is $600.

Value means the full actual consideration paid or to be paid, including any lien on the property. For a gift, a nominal-price deed or a swap, the statute uses the estimated price the property would bring on the open market between a willing buyer and seller (s. 77.21). Under s. 77.24, 20 percent of what a county collects stays with the county and the rest goes to the state.

Several transfers are exempt under s. 77.25. The ones sellers and heirs run into most often are:

  • a conveyance by will, descent or survivorship;
  • a foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder or land contract seller;
  • a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments;
  • a transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration;
  • a conveyance of real estate worth $1,000 or less;
  • a deed that only gives or releases security for a debt.

The register has no duty to decide whether an exemption is valid, so state the reason correctly on the return. State law also bars a city, village, town or county from charging its own fee on a conveyance the state fee exempts (s. 77.256).

What do you need to bring or mail to record a deed in Milwaukee County?

You need the signed original deed, a transfer return receipt, and payment. Wisconsin law says every conveyance offered for recording must come with the return described in s. 77.22(2), and the register will not accept the deed without it. On January 12, 2026, the Department of Revenue announced that the transfer return is available in its My Tax Account system, where filers need no username or password.

  • The original document or documents, completed before you submit them.
  • The transfer return receipt for any conveyance document, or the exemption reason shown on it.
  • A check payable to the Register of Deeds, or cash, for the $30 fee and any transfer fee.
  • A return name and address on the document, because the original comes back by mail.

The document itself has to meet the content rules in Wis. Stat. 706.05. It needs the signatures the law requires and must identify the land and the parties so the office can index it. A document that is to be indexed in the real estate records, modifies an original mortgage or land contract, or is a subordination agreement must carry the full legal description, and a modification must also give the document number of the original mortgage or land contract.

The register does not prepare documents or carry blank deed forms, and cannot say whether a document is legally sound. Owners can draft their own or hire an attorney or title company. Questions about the return itself go to the Department of Revenue, which the county page lists at (608) 266-1594 or eRETR@revenue.wi.gov.

How long does recording take in Milwaukee County?

Documents are recorded within three to five business days, in the order they are received, and the original is mailed back within one to two weeks. The office says documents are not recorded immediately, so leave room for this window before a closing date. For questions about a pending document, email RODrecordings@milwaukeecountywi.gov or call (414) 278-4005.

If you are selling to a cash buyer who wants a quick close, ask the closing agent when the deed will go to the Register of Deeds and which return exemption, if any, applies to your transfer.

How do you remove a deceased owner from a Milwaukee County deed?

You record a termination of decedent's interest. For a deed that names both spouses, the county lists the Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110), the transfer return with the exemption under s. 77.25(11) for a transfer by will, descent or survivorship, a copy of the recorded ownership deed, and a $30 fee. The county says it no longer requires a copy of the real estate tax bill or the death certificate.

When a transfer on death document was recorded and the owner has died, the steps are the same except the form is TOD-110 and the exemption is s. 77.25(11m). Forms and instructions are on the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association site. Anyone selling an inherited Milwaukee County house should ask the title company whether this step is needed before closing.

To change ownership in any other way, such as adding or removing a name, a new deed has to be drafted and recorded with its transfer return. The office cannot draft it for you.

What is Property Fraud Alert in Milwaukee County?

It is a free online service that emails an owner when their exact name appears as grantor or grantee on a document recorded in the Register of Deeds office. It does not stop fraud. It gives an early warning, so an owner can act quickly if a deed or mortgage shows up that they never signed.

Sign up if you own a house you do not live in, such as a rental, an inherited property waiting for sale, or a vacant home.

What is the Milwaukee County housing market like for sellers?

Census Bureau figures show a county split almost evenly between owners and renters. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied housing rate was 49.9 percent, the median value of owner-occupied homes was $230,700, and median gross rent was $1,101. The county had 392,399 households and 429,425 housing units as of July 1, 2025.

The county covers 1,189 square miles in total, but only 241 of those are land. The rest is Lake Michigan, which is why Milwaukee County has the highest density in Wisconsin at 3,890.5 people per square mile of land in 2020. The city of Milwaukee is the county seat, and the next largest places by 2020 population include West Allis, Wauwatosa, Greenfield, Oak Creek and Franklin.

These are county averages. Ask the treasurer of the city or village where your house sits for its tax bill before you set a price.

Where can Milwaukee County owners get legal help with deeds?

The Register of Deeds cannot give legal advice, but the county page lists two places to start. The Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinic gives free, confidential and brief legal advice at House of Peace Community Center, 1702 W. Walnut Street, on Tuesdays from 4 to 6 p.m. (sign-in begins at 3:30 p.m.), phone (414) 933-1300. The Lawyer Referral and Information Service takes calls Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

More questions about Milwaukee County, WI Register of Deeds

How much does the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?

The recording fee is $30 per document, regardless of page count, with a separate transfer fee on most sales. Plats cost $25 to $50 to record, and a condominium plat adds a $100 review fee paid by separate check. The office takes cash, checks and money orders only.

How much is the transfer fee when I sell a house in Milwaukee County?

It is 30 cents per $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, set by Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $250,000 sale carries a fee of $750. The seller owes it, and it is collected when the deed is recorded. Exempt transfers, such as one by will or a foreclosure, owe nothing.

Can I record a deed in Milwaukee County without a transfer return?

No. Wisconsin law requires the return with every conveyance offered for recording, and the Milwaukee County office lists the receipt as required for all conveyance documents. If the transfer is exempt, the return still records the exemption reason.

How do I get my recorded deed back from Milwaukee County?

The office mails the original recorded document to the name and return address on it. Recording takes three to five business days, and the mail return takes one to two weeks. Buy a certified copy at recording if you need proof sooner.

Does the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds handle property tax bills?

No. It records documents and collects the transfer fee. Tax bills for Milwaukee County properties come from the municipality where the house sits, so ask that city or village treasurer for balances and payoffs.

Where does the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds record deeds?

The Manitowoc County Register of Deeds sits in the county courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. Every deed, mortgage and satisfaction on a Manitowoc County house is recorded there, and the office keeps the permanent index of those records.

Hours on the county page are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. The real estate page adds that documents are recorded daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, so plan to arrive well before 4:00 PM. The main phone number is 920-683-4660.

Staff here cannot draft a deed or give legal advice. If your sale involves an inherited house, a land contract or a title problem, a Wisconsin attorney or the title company handling the closing should prepare the paperwork before it reaches the counter.

What is Manitowoc County like for someone selling a house?

Manitowoc County covers 1,494 square miles on the Lake Michigan shore, but only 589 of those square miles are land. The other 905 square miles (61 percent) are water. The county was created in 1836 and organized in 1848, and the city of Manitowoc is the county seat. Since 2021 much of the northern half of the Wisconsin Shipwreck Coast National Marine Sanctuary has lain off its coast.

The Census Bureau counted 81,359 residents in 2020 and estimated 81,710 for July 2025, a gain of about 0.4 percent. About 24.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, a share that matters when a family sells a parent's house.

  • Housing units: 38,298 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.1 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $186,900.
  • Median gross rent: $797 a month.
  • Median household income: $69,148.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 152.

With a median home value under $190,000, the $30 recording fee and the transfer fee on a typical Manitowoc County sale are small next to repair and carrying costs. The paperwork rules are the same for a $90,000 house as for a $400,000 one.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Manitowoc County?

Recording one deed costs $30 under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), and the fee is due in advance. Copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each page after that, plus $1 to certify a copy. These base amounts are set by state law, so they apply in every Wisconsin county.

Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added pageWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)

The county posts a separate fee schedule link on its real estate page. Ask the Register of Deeds for the current office schedule if you need anything beyond these statutory items, such as search or special handling charges.

How does the Wisconsin transfer fee work on a Manitowoc County sale?

The seller (the grantor) owes a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value, or fraction of $100, under Wis. Stat. 77.22. On a $186,900 sale, roughly the county median home value, that comes to about $561. The Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is submitted and writes the amount on the face of the deed.

Twenty percent of the fee stays with the county and the rest goes to the state, according to Wis. Stat. 77.24. The office does not check whether your stated price is correct. Section 77.22 says the register has no duty to determine the true value or to test an exemption claim, so the return you sign carries your own statement under the law.

Some conveyances owe no fee. Section 77.25 lists exemptions such as these:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration.
  • A transfer of real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • A deed under foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder or land contract seller.
  • A transfer on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

When a deed is exempt, the reason must be stated on its face by citing the right subsection of 77.25.

What must a deed include before Manitowoc County will record it?

The office may refuse a document that does not substantially follow the standard format in Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m). The statute asks for the following:

  • A clear document title placed between 0.5 inch and 6 inches from the top of page one.
  • A blank 3 inch by 3 inch space in the upper right corner of the first page for the recording stamp.
  • Return information on page one, unless the document is recorded electronically.
  • White paper of at least 20 pound weight, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Black, blue or red ink, with pages not hinged or joined along the top or sides.
  • The name of the person or agency that drafted the document.
  • Clearly written or typed names for the grantor, grantee and any notary.

A document that contains an individual's Social Security number cannot be recorded under subsection (1m). Strip any such number before you submit the deed. If a group of documents is presented as one transaction and one of them fails the format rules, the register may send the whole set back unrecorded.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Manitowoc County?

Yes. The Manitowoc County real estate page lists four e-recording providers and says each has a sign-up process: Simplifile at 713-210-4323, Hopdox at 385-501-5103, Indecomm at 651-765-6400 and EPN at 888-325-3365. If a title company or closing attorney handles your sale, ask whether it will submit the deed through one of these providers.

Every deed also needs a Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return (ERETR). The county page tells filers to save the return before pressing submit and to print the receipt, because the receipt must travel with the original deed when it is recorded at the office. Leave the page without printing it and you have to file the return again.

How can an owner guard against deed fraud in Manitowoc County?

Sign up for the free notification service the Register of Deeds offers. It tells you when a document is recorded against your name or property so you can confirm it is genuine. The county describes real estate fraud as rare in Wisconsin, and the alert costs nothing and takes one call to 920-683-4660.

The service is especially useful for owners who live out of the area, hold an inherited house that sits empty, or are waiting on a sale to close. Once your own deed is recorded, you can use the same alert to watch for anything filed afterward.

More questions about Manitowoc County, WI Register of Deeds

What is the address of the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds?

It is in the Manitowoc County Courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. The phone number is 920-683-4660. Hours are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30, and documents are recorded daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Manitowoc County?

The statutory recording fee is $30 per document, payable in advance under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag). Add the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value if the sale is not exempt. Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, with $1 more to certify.

Do I need to file anything with the state before the deed is recorded?

Yes. File a Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return, then print the receipt. The Manitowoc County page says the receipt must accompany the original deed when you record at the Register of Deeds. Only conveyances exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(1) or (10m) skip the return.

Does a transfer of an inherited house owe the transfer fee?

Usually not. A conveyance by will, descent or survivorship is exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). A later sale of the inherited house to a buyer is a different conveyance and carries the fee based on the price. Ask the Register of Deeds or a Wisconsin attorney how to document the first transfer.

Can I record a deed in Manitowoc County by e-recording?

Yes. The county lists Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm and EPN as e-recording providers, each with its own sign-up phone number. Ask your title company or closing attorney whether it will submit the deed through one of them.

The deed also needs the name of the drafter and the name and mailing address of the person it should be returned to. If an out-of-state form is the only one you have, the county says you may attach a cover sheet that supplies the title, return address and parcel number in the proper places.

What formatting rules apply to Marathon County deeds?

Wisconsin Statute 59.43(2m) sets a standard document format, and the Marathon County office applies it. A document that misses the standard can be refused. The county lists these points:

  • Leave the upper right corner blank, at least 3 inches by 3 inches, for the recording stamp.
  • Put the name and return address directly under that area, or on the left within the top 3 inches.
  • Place the parcel identifier number directly under the return address.
  • Keep the title inside the top 3 inches, outside the blank corner.
  • Use white, standard weight, letter or legal size paper with black ink so the page scans.
  • Keep a top margin of at least half an inch on every page and other margins of at least a quarter inch.
  • Do not hinge the pages.

State law also bars the office from recording a document that contains an individual's Social Security number, so remove it before you send the deed.

How do I search Marathon County land records online?

Since September 3, 2019, Marathon County has used the Ascent Land Records Suite from Transcendent Technologies, and land and tax information is posted at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords. The real estate index can also be searched free in LandShark. Viewing or printing a recorded document there costs a fee.

Surveys are held by the county surveyor, whose number is 715-261-6000. The surveyor's online folders cover benchmarks, section summaries, plats of survey and tie sheets, sorted by town and range. A pre-sale check of the recorded chain of title and any survey is worth doing before you sign a contract.

Records requests follow the same rule as other Wisconsin government records. The county page says the presumption is that a record is open for public inspection, and a denial must come with specific reasons. A person who is denied can start a court action to compel disclosure.

Which Marathon County forms help with inherited property?

The Marathon County recording page lists several forms that come up when an owner has died: a Personal Representative Deed, a Designation of TOD Beneficiary, a Termination of Decedent's Interest form with instructions, a Quit Claim Deed form and a Warrant Deed. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt from the state transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11), and the exemption reason must be written on the deed.

A sale by the heirs to a buyer afterward is a new conveyance. The fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22 applies to it at 30 cents per $100 of value, with the seller owing it.

What is the phone number for the Marathon County Register of Deeds?

The phone number is 715-261-1470, and the fax is 715-261-1488. The office is at 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Call ahead for current hours, because the county posts temporary schedule changes.

How much is the recording fee in Marathon County?

It is $30 per document for real estate records. Certification adds $1.00 per filed document, and copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page. Any state transfer fee is paid in addition.

Can I mail a deed to the Marathon County Register of Deeds?

Yes. Send the deed, the printed transfer return receipt and a $30 check payable to Register of Deeds to 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Add any transfer fee and an email address. Documents are returned electronically unless you enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

Is there a Wisconsin transfer fee when I sell a Marathon County house?

Yes, unless an exemption applies. The seller owes 30 cents for each $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22. For a $219,600 sale, near the county median home value, the fee is about $659. Exempt transfers include those by will, descent or survivorship.

Use LandShark for the real estate index, which is free to search, and the Ascent land records site at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords for land and tax information. Viewing or printing a recorded document through LandShark costs a fee.

Columbia County by the numbers

Where is the Columbia County Register of Deeds, and what does it do?

The Columbia County Register of Deeds is at 112 E. Edgewater St. in Portage, Wisconsin 53901. Christine Clark is the Register of Deeds, and the office phone is (608) 742-9677.

The counter is open from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and genealogy searches run from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. The county fax is (608) 742-9875. The office is the official county repository for real estate records, including deeds, land contracts, mortgages, UCC filings, subdivision and condominium plats, certified survey maps, lis pendens and annexations. It also keeps vital records such as births, deaths and marriages. Wisconsin set up the office in 1836, and the 1848 state constitution made it a permanent part of county government.

Official certified copies of recorded documents come only from this office. For a seller, the office matters at the end of the deal: the deed that moves ownership to the buyer is recorded here, along with the electronic transfer return and fee.

What does it cost to record a deed in Columbia County?

Recording a deed costs $30 per document, no matter how many pages it has. The same $30 applies to mortgages, land contracts and satisfactions.

ItemFee
Deed, mortgage, land contract or satisfaction$30 per document, any number of pages
Subdivision, cemetery or condominium plat$50 per plat
Transportation project plat$30 per plat
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page, plus $1 for a certified copy
Plat copy$5 per page of a plat-size copy, $3 per page of a condominium plat
Real estate transfer fee$3.00 per $1,000 of value, rounded to the next higher hundred

Source: Columbia County Register of Deeds, Real Estate Fees.

The first page of every recorded document must have a blank 3 by 3 inch area in the upper right corner. If it does not, add a cover page. Check the current fee schedule with the office before you mail a check, since fees can change.

How does the Wisconsin transfer fee work for a Columbia County sale?

The grantor, usually the seller, owes a fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction under Wisconsin Statute 77.22(1), and the register collects it when the deed is submitted for recording. The county's schedule states the same rate as $3.00 per $1,000, rounded up to the next hundred.

A transfer return is required for all conveyances except the oldest exemption category, for conveyances before October 1, 1969. The return must show the value even when the sale is exempt from the fee. Under state law the return is filed electronically, and the deed cannot be accepted for recording without the completed return and the fee. The register does not decide whether the stated value is right or whether an exemption is valid.

Statute 77.25 lists the exemptions. Several come up in home sales and estates:

  • A conveyance by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration.
  • A transfer under a foreclosure, or a deed in lieu, to a mortgage holder or land contract seller.
  • A conveyance of real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

Twenty percent of fees collected stays with the county, and the rest goes to the state. The reason for any exemption must be stated on the face of the deed, referring to the right subsection of 77.25.

What format must a deed meet to be recorded in Columbia County?

It must follow the Wisconsin standard document format, which Wisconsin Statute 59.43(2m) requires. The format took effect on September 1, 1996 under Wisconsin Act 110, and most office supply stores sell forms that meet it.

The register lists these format rules:

  • Leave the upper right corner blank, at least 3 by 3 inches, for the recording stamp.
  • Put the name and return address directly under that area, or on the left side within the top 3 inches.
  • Place the parcel identifier number directly under the return address.
  • Put the document title in the top 3 inches, outside the blank corner.
  • Use white, standard-weight letter or legal paper and ink that scans well. The format page lists black, blue or red, and the checklist asks for black.
  • Keep margins at least 1/2 inch at the top of every page and 1/4 inch elsewhere. Do not use hinged pages.

A document from outside Wisconsin can take a cover sheet with the title, return address and parcel number, attached as the first page.

What else does the Columbia County register require before recording?

A complete legal description, original signatures with a notary's authentication and valid commission date, and the correct fee. The register also requires the name of the document drafter.

  • The document must refer to land inside Columbia County.
  • The title, return address, party names and legal description must be legible and reproducible.
  • An electronic Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return is required for conveyances. For deeds and land contracts it must show the proper fee or exemption number.
  • Several mortgages, assignments or satisfactions may not be put on the same instrument.

The cut-off time for receiving real estate documents is 3:30 p.m. A document presented after 3:30 p.m. is recorded the next business day. If a closing depends on same-day recording, plan to deliver the package early in the afternoon.

How do you search Columbia County land records?

The office offers online access to recorded documents through Fidlar Software products named Laredo and Tapestry, and its site also describes xPedite. The county's tract index begins January 1, 2006, so searches for earlier real estate documents require a grantor and grantee search.

The register's index is a working index. The office cautions that it may contain errors, omissions or later changes, so results should not be relied on in court or administrative proceedings about title or transfer of property. For an official copy, contact the office at (608) 742-9677.

Property taxes sit with the Columbia County Treasurer. Ask the county treasurer for any balance on the parcel before the sale closes, and ask the treasurer or the title company how the balance will be paid from the proceeds.

What does Columbia County look like for a seller?

Columbia County is a mostly rural county north of Madison. Portage is the county seat and largest city, and the county was created in 1846 as part of Wisconsin Territory. The 2020 census counted 58,490 people, and the county belongs to the Madison metropolitan area.

It covers 796 square miles, of which 766 are land and 30 are water. The highest point is in the Baraboo Range near Durward's Glen, at 1,480 feet above sea level. Its cities are Columbus (partly in Dodge County), Lodi, Portage and Wisconsin Dells (partly in Adams, Juneau and Sauk counties). Dane, Sauk, Dodge, Marquette, Green Lake, Juneau and Adams counties touch its borders.

In 2020 the county had 26,565 housing units, of which 10.1% were vacant, and 74.6% of occupied units were owned. About 66.2% of residents lived in rural areas.

More questions about Columbia County, WI Register of Deeds

How much does the Columbia County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?

The charge is $30 per document regardless of the number of pages. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and satisfactions all use that rate. The state transfer fee is separate.

What is the Columbia County transfer fee rate?

The rate is $3.00 per $1,000 of value, rounded to the next higher hundred. That equals 30 cents per $100 under Wisconsin Statute 77.22(1), and the grantor owes it unless an exemption applies.

What time does the Columbia County Register of Deeds stop accepting documents for the day?

The cut-off for real estate documents is 3:30 p.m. Anything presented after that is recorded on the next business day. The office is open from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Do I need a transfer return to record a deed in Columbia County?

Yes, for almost every conveyance. The county requires an electronic Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return with the fee or an exemption number, and the value must be shown even for an exempt transfer.

Where do I get a certified copy of a recorded Columbia County deed?

Only from the Columbia County Register of Deeds in Portage. Certified copies cost $2 for the first page, $1 for each added page and $1 more for the certification. Call (608) 742-9677 for help.

Portage County by the numbers

What does the Portage County Register of Deeds do when you sell a house?

The Portage County Register of Deeds records the deed that moves a house from you to the buyer, and it collects the state transfer fee at the moment the deed is submitted. Nothing in the sale is public record until that office accepts the document. Portage County is in central Wisconsin, with Stevens Point as the county seat and largest city, so most sellers deal with the office that serves the Stevens Point courthouse area.

Under Wis. Stat. s. 77.22, the register collects the fee when the instrument of conveyance comes in for recording. The register also writes the fee amount on the face of the deed before recording it. The register has no duty to decide whether the stated price is right or whether an exemption is valid, so the paperwork you file has to be accurate before it arrives.

The county page for the Register of Deeds/Land Description office describes its job as official record keeping for real estate, personal property and vital statistics. Ask that office directly for current hours, accepted payment types and whether it takes documents by mail.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Portage County, Wisconsin?

Recording a standard document costs $30 under s. 59.43(2)(ag), plus a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value. On a $180,000 sale, the transfer fee works out to $540, so the combined charge is $570 for a single deed. A few document types carry a different recording charge, so confirm the total with the office before you mail a check.

ItemAmountSource
Recording a document$30Wis. Stat. s. 59.43(2)(ag)
Real estate transfer fee30 cents per $100 of valueWis. Stat. s. 77.22(1)
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added pageWis. Stat. s. 59.43(2)(b)
Certifying a copy$1 extraWis. Stat. s. 59.43(2)(b)
Transfer fee on a value of $1,000 or lessExemptWis. Stat. s. 77.25(13)

The statute defines value as the full actual consideration, including any lien on the property. On a land contract, value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay. Of each transfer fee collected, the county keeps 20 percent and the rest goes to the state (s. 77.24).

What is the eRETR and who files it?

The electronic real estate transfer return, or eRETR, is the Wisconsin Department of Revenue form that must be completed for a conveyance. Portage County states that you prepare it on the Department of Revenue website, print the receipt, and send the receipt with the deed and the fees to the Register of Deeds. Both the grantor and the grantee sign the return under s. 77.22(1).

The statute says the return must be filed electronically, and the secretary of revenue may waive that only after a written hardship application. Without a completed return and the fee, the register cannot accept the deed for recording. A title company or closing attorney normally files it for you, and the seller should check that the sale price shown matches the purchase contract.

  • Sale price and any liens assumed by the buyer count toward value.
  • Both parties are named on the return, so the buyer's information has to be ready before you record.
  • Keep the printed eRETR receipt with the original deed until the office returns the recorded copy.

Which Portage County transfers skip the transfer fee?

Section 77.25 lists the conveyances that owe no fee, and when one applies the reason has to be written on the face of the deed by citing the subsection. Courts read these exemptions narrowly, so a case that only resembles one of them should be treated as taxable until a title professional says otherwise.

  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship (s. 77.25(11)), which matters for inherited houses.
  • Transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration (s. 77.25(8)).
  • A foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder or land contract seller (s. 77.25(14)).
  • A deed that corrects or confirms an earlier recorded conveyance for nominal or no consideration (s. 77.25(3)).
  • A conveyance on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments (s. 77.25(4)).

No city, village, town or county may charge its own fee on a conveyance that the state exempts (s. 77.256). If a return is not required for an exempt transfer, s. 77.255 says so for the listed cases.

How must a deed be formatted before the register accepts it?

The register may refuse a document that does not substantially follow the standard format in s. 59.43(2m). The title of the document must sit between half an inch and six inches from the top of the first page. The first page must also leave a blank space of at least 3 inches by 3 inches in the upper right corner, inside the margins, for recording information, and a document without that space may not be recorded.

These rules explain why a deed copied from an old form or printed from an online template is sometimes returned. Have the title company or attorney handling the sale review the final deed before anyone signs.

How do Portage County property taxes affect a sale?

Portage County collects most real estate taxes through the County Treasurer at 1516 Church Street in Stevens Point, phone (715) 346-1348, open Monday through Friday 7:30 am to 4:30 pm. Taxes are due in two installments, January 31 and July 31, and the county treasurer takes payments for 23 of the 28 municipalities on the first installment and 27 of 28 on the second. The City of Stevens Point collects all three of its installments for the current year, so a Stevens Point seller pays the city, not the county.

Towns of Almond, Belmont and Lanark and the Village of Milladore collect their own first installment. Ask the right treasurer for the exact payoff figure before closing.

  • Payments made by check or cash at the window or by mail carry no fee.
  • Card payments carry the vendor fees the county lists: 2.39 percent for credit cards, $3.95 for online debit, and $1.50 for an electronic check.
  • The county does not mail a second-installment reminder, and it does not offer payment plans on delinquent taxes, although it takes payments of any amount.

What happens if Portage County taxes on a house go unpaid?

A missed installment ends the right to pay in installments, and interest of 1.5 percent per month starts on the unpaid balance after the grace period. The county says taxes become delinquent on the sixth business day after the due date. Statute s. 74.11(7) and (8) set that five working day grace window for each installment.

If taxes are still unpaid on September 1, the county issues a tax certificate and sends a notice of issuance. The owner then has two years to pay that year's balance before the county starts a tax deed foreclosure. The county's Tax Deed Land Sale page showed a 2026 online auction that ran September 17 to October 8, 2026, with six parcels and minimum bids from $1,000 to $149,200. That sale is over, and the same page lists future sales.

Owners who are behind on taxes while a foreclosure is in process can ask the Foundation for Rural Housing, which the county names as a source of funds for delinquent taxes. Its numbers on the county page are 608-238-3448 and 888-400-5974.

Which credits lower a Portage County tax bill?

Three credits appear on Portage County bills. The school levy tax credit is applied automatically to every bill, and the first dollar credit is applied automatically to parcels that contain an improvement. The lottery and gaming credit applies to a primary residence and must be claimed, and it can be claimed on only one parcel.

The Treasurer's page lists the yearly real estate ratios, first dollar credits, lottery credits and mill rates for 2021 through 2025.

Where can you look up a Portage County parcel and its recorded documents?

Portage County runs an online land records site at landinfo.co.portage.wi.gov, which the Treasurer's Office also uses for tax searches and online payments. The county advises searching by parcel number alone, matching the format on the bill, since extra search terms return fewer results. You can also search by property address or by first and last name.

Pull the parcel record before you list the house so the legal owner, mailing address and tax status all match the deed you plan to sign.

What does Portage County look like for a seller?

Portage County covers 801 square miles of land and 22 square miles of water. The 2020 census counted 70,377 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 71,943. Wikipedia reports that 63.4 percent of residents live in urban areas, 68.4 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the median age is 38.8.

Neighbors include Marathon, Shawano, Waupaca, Waushara, Adams and Wood counties. The county has 28 municipalities, from the City of Stevens Point to small towns such as Alban, Hull and New Hope. The register records the deed for all of them, while each town, village or city decides who collects its first tax installment.

More questions about Portage County, WI Register of Deeds

Where do I record a deed for a Portage County house?

Record it with the Portage County Register of Deeds/Land Description office. Send the signed deed, the eRETR receipt and the fees together, and call the office first to confirm hours and payment types.

How much is the transfer fee in Portage County?

It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, set by Wis. Stat. s. 77.22(1). A $240,000 sale would owe $720, in addition to the $30 recording charge for the deed.

Do I need to file an electronic transfer return?

Yes, for a conveyance of real estate that is not exempt. Portage County says the eRETR is prepared on the Department of Revenue website and the printed receipt goes to the register with the deed.

Is there a transfer fee when I inherit a house in Portage County?

A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt under s. 77.25(11). Sale of the inherited house by the heir is a new conveyance and owes the fee.

When are Portage County property taxes due?

The first installment is due January 31 and the second July 31. The City of Stevens Point collects its own installments, and a few towns and one village collect the first installment themselves, so check your bill coupon.

Fond Du Lac County by the numbers

Where do I record a deed in Fond du Lac County?

You record it with the Fond du Lac County Register of Deeds, 160 S Macy St, 1st Floor, Fond du Lac, WI. The mailing address is PO Box 509, Fond du Lac, WI 54936-0509, and the phone number is (920) 929-3018. The county site lists James M. Krebs as the Register of Deeds.

The office is open 7:45 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday, except holidays. Real estate documents are recorded between 7:45 am and 3:30 pm. A deed that arrives after 3:30 pm is recorded the next business day, so a seller who wants a same-day recording date should deliver the paperwork before that cutoff.

The office takes real estate documents three ways: e-recording, mail, and in-person delivery. Title companies, banks and law firms usually use e-recording. The county lists Simplifile, CSC eRecording Solutions, Indecomm Global Services, eRecording Partners Network and hopdox as the vendors it works with. A homeowner selling without a title company can mail the deed or walk it in. After recording, the original goes back to the return address printed on the document.

What must a deed include before the register accepts it?

A deed that misses a formatting rule can be sent back, which delays the closing. The county's recording requirements page, which cites Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m), lists the points that cause most rejections:

  • A blank 3 inch by 3 inch space in the upper right corner of the first page for the recording stamp.
  • Top margins of at least half an inch, and side and bottom margins of at least a quarter inch on the first page.
  • White paper of standard 20 pound weight, letter or legal size, with no hinged pages.
  • A return name and address, and the name of the person who drafted the document.
  • Original signatures, plus an attorney's authentication or a notary's certificate of acknowledgment with a valid commission date.
  • No Social Security number anywhere on the document. Under 59.43(1m)(a) the register may not record a document that contains one.
  • A legible, reproducible image of every page.

The county says its list covers the most common requirements and is not exhaustive. For an unusual instrument, such as a correction deed or a plat, call the office at (920) 929-3018 before you send it.

How much does recording cost in Fond du Lac County?

A standard real estate document costs $30 to record, no matter how many pages it has. Plats are $50. The $30 figure matches Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), and the $50 plat fee matches 59.43(2)(h). Fees are payable in advance by the party asking for the service under 59.43(2g)(a).

The county fee schedule also lists copy charges, which come up when a buyer or lender wants proof of what was recorded:

  • Standard copies: $2.00 for the first page of a document and $1.00 for each additional page of that document.
  • Certified copies: add $1.00 to the standard copy charge.

Recording is separate from the state transfer fee described below. A seller's closing statement normally shows both lines, and the register collects the transfer fee at the same time the deed is submitted.

How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Fond du Lac County sale?

The fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value, or fraction of $100, which works out to $3 per $1,000. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) puts the fee on the grantor, so the seller pays it. For a sale, value means the full price paid or to be paid, including the amount of any lien on the property. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, it is the estimated open-market price (77.21(3)). On a land contract, the value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay.

The register collects the fee when the deed is submitted and writes the amount on the face of the deed. If no fee is due, the deed has to state the reason by citing the matching subsection of 77.25. The register has no duty to check the value or confirm that an exemption applies, so the filer carries that responsibility. Under 77.24, 20 percent of collected fees stays with the county and the rest goes to the state.

Which transfers are exempt from the transfer fee?

Section 77.25 lists the exemptions, and courts read them narrowly. Several apply to families selling, inheriting or reorganizing property in Fond du Lac County:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship (77.25(11)).
  • A transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration (77.25(8)), and between an individual and a domestic partner (77.25(8n)).
  • A deed to a mortgage holder under a foreclosure or a deed in lieu of foreclosure (77.25(14)).
  • A deed that confirms, corrects or reforms a conveyance already recorded, when it carries nominal or no consideration (77.25(3)).
  • A transfer from a trustee to a beneficiary without actual consideration (77.25(9)), and a transfer to a trust if a transfer to its beneficiary would be exempt (77.25(16)).
  • Real estate worth $1,000 or less (77.25(13)).

An ordinary arm's-length sale of a house does not fit any of these. If you think a sale qualifies, have the closing attorney or title company cite the exact subsection on the deed.

What is the real estate transfer return?

The transfer return is an electronic form from the Wisconsin Department of Revenue that must be filed for any conveyance of an ownership interest in real estate. You complete it on the state website, print the receipt, and send the receipt and any fee to the Register of Deeds along with the deed. The register will not accept the deed without it. The form is signed by both grantor and grantee under 77.22(1), and the return form is prescribed by the Department of Revenue under 77.22(2).

The county's page notes that the Department of Revenue was moving the return into its My Tax Account system on January 12, 2026, so use the link on the county page to reach the current filing screen. Questions about the return itself go to RETR@wisconsin.gov. Questions about whether the register has received a recorded deed go to the county office.

How can I search or monitor Fond du Lac County land records?

The county's LandShark system lets you search and buy copies of recorded deeds, mortgages and easements going back to 1839. Public terminals in the office allow in-person research. For older work, the tract index book images cover the period before June 1, 1994, and the grantor and grantee name index book images run from 1835 through 1985.

Land Notification is a free county service that sends an email or text message when a document is recorded against your name, your business name or a parcel identification number. It exists to catch property fraud early, which matters for owners of vacant lots, inherited houses and rentals that nobody visits often. Call (920) 929-3018 with questions about setting up alerts.

What should a Fond du Lac County seller know about the area?

Fond du Lac County covers 766 square miles at the southern end of Lake Winnebago, with the city of Fond du Lac as county seat. Wikipedia counts 33 municipalities: 3 cities (Fond du Lac, Ripon and Waupun, which lies mostly in Dodge County), 21 towns and 9 villages. The county was created in 1836 and organized in 1844.

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 104,669 and the 2025 housing unit count at 46,496. About 70.7 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, the median home value is $222,800, median household income is $74,275, and median gross rent is $960 (2020 to 2024 figures). The county issued 190 building permits in 2025.

Taxes also come up at a Fond du Lac County closing. When a deed is recorded in a calendar year, Wis. Stat. 74.15 sets a default split of that year's taxes if the contract is silent: the grantor pays the grantee one-twelfth of last year's assessed taxes per elapsed month, and a sale after the 15th counts that month too. Most purchase contracts replace that default with their own proration language, so read the contract and ask the title company for the final figure.

More questions about Fond du Lac County, WI Register of Deeds

What time does the Fond du Lac County Register of Deeds close?

The office is open until 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, but real estate documents are recorded only between 7:45 am and 3:30 pm. Anything received after 3:30 pm is recorded on the next business day.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Fond du Lac County?

It costs $30 per standard real estate document, regardless of page count, and $50 for a plat. Copies are $2.00 for the first page and $1.00 for each added page, plus $1.00 to certify.

Who pays the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?

The seller, who is the grantor, pays it. The rate is 30 cents per $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, under Wis. Stat. 77.22(1). A $200,000 sale produces a $600 fee unless an exemption in 77.25 applies.

Do I need a title company to record a deed in Fond du Lac County?

No. The register accepts documents by e-recording, mail and in-person delivery, and the county says you may fill out deed forms yourself or hire an attorney. The deed still has to meet the format rules and arrive with the electronic transfer return receipt and the fees.

Can I be alerted if someone records a document against my property?

Yes. Land Notification is a free county service that sends email or text alerts when a document is recorded under your name or against a parcel identification number you enter. Sign up through the Register of Deeds page.

Marinette County by the numbers

Where is the Marinette County Register of Deeds?

The Marinette County Register of Deeds is at 1926 Hall Ave, Marinette, WI 54143. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. The main phone number is 715-732-7551 and the fax is 715-732-7556. Packages sent by FedEx or UPS go to a separate address, 1925 Ella Court, Marinette, WI 54143.

The office describes its job as being the official county repository for real estate instruments and vital records, with archival storage and convenient access to them. It also collects and accounts for fees under Wisconsin statutes. For a house sale, that means the deed, any mortgage payoff paperwork and the transfer return all pass through this counter.

What is Marinette County like for a home seller?

Marinette County is large and thinly settled. It covers 1,550 square miles, of which 1,399 are land and 151 (9.7 percent) are water, making it the third largest Wisconsin county by land area and the fifth largest in total area. Part of its edge touches Lake Michigan. The Peshtigo and Menominee rivers, many lakes and forests, and a large snowmobile trail network draw visitors, and Dave's Falls near Amberg is one of the county's waterfalls. The county's own website calls Marinette County the Waterfalls Capital of Wisconsin.

The Census Bureau counted 41,872 people in 2020 and estimated 42,574 for July 2025, up 1.7 percent. The 2020 census showed 29,189 housing units and a vacancy figure of 35.8 percent. By comparison, the same census page for Marathon County shows 5.5 percent and the one for Milwaukee County shows 7.2 percent. About 60.8 percent of residents lived in rural areas.

  • Median age: 49.3 years (2020 census), with 28.3 percent of residents 65 or older.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 81.6 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $158,600.
  • Median gross rent: $795 a month.
  • Median household income: $63,809.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 215.

The city of Marinette is the county seat, and the county belongs to the Marinette, WI to MI Micropolitan Statistical Area. Crivitz Municipal Airport serves the county. Workers face a mean commute of 21.1 minutes, and the Census Bureau puts the poverty rate at 11.8 percent.

What does it cost to record a deed in Marinette County?

The office follows Wisconsin's statutory fees. Recording a document is $30, and all fees are payable in advance by the person asking for the service under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2g). Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 per added page, plus $1 to certify one. The county's own fee page, titled User Fees, sits under the Register of Deeds menu, and the office can tell you about any other charge.

What does the Marinette County office do with a deed once it arrives?

State law spells out the register's duties in Wis. Stat. 59.43(1c). They include the following:

  • Record each document in the order it is received.
  • Stamp it with the date, hour and minute of recording, which is prima facie evidence of when it was recorded.
  • Give it a unique number that follows the number of the previous document in its series.
  • Keep the originals, images and indexes permanently.
  • Note on a conveyance the transfer fee paid, or cite the reason it is exempt.
  • Deliver the recorded document to the person you name, once you provide adequate postage.

The endorsement matters when two documents reach the same property close together, such as a deed and a mortgage. A seller with a closing date should get the deed to the office early, since the stamp records the order in which documents arrived.

How does the transfer fee work on a Marinette County sale?

The seller owes 30 cents for each $100 of value, or fraction of $100, on a conveyance that is not exempt. On a $158,600 sale, about the county median home value, the fee comes to about $476. For a land contract the value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay, and for a gift or exchange it is the estimated open market price.

Buyer and seller must both sign a transfer return. Since July 1, 2009 the state has required filing it electronically unless the Department of Revenue waives that for hardship, and the county site lists Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Returns on the Register of Deeds menu. Completed returns and the fees go to the county treasurer monthly by the 15th, and 20 percent of the money stays with the county. A city, village, town or county cannot add its own fee to a conveyance that the state fee exempts.

Which Marinette County transfers owe no state fee?

Wis. Stat. 77.25 lists the exempt conveyances. A few that matter for private owners are these:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A deed from a trustee to a beneficiary, or between agent and principal, without actual consideration.
  • A transfer between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal or no consideration.
  • A conveyance made only to give or release security for a debt.
  • A deed on foreclosure, or in place of it, to the mortgage holder or the land contract seller.
  • A deed that completes a land contract when the proper fee was paid on the contract.

Exemptions are read narrowly, so a transfer that is close to one of these but not squarely inside it may still owe the fee. Ask a Wisconsin attorney if your situation is unclear.

Can I record electronically or search Marinette County records online?

Yes to both. The county lists two electronic recording services: CSC (Corporation Services Corp), reachable at 866-403-5272, and Simplifile at 800-460-5657. Online, LandShark provides access to documents recorded in the Marinette County Register of Deeds office from 1990 forward. You can register and view the index at no charge. The site offers one option for daily users, such as title firms that need to view and buy images, and another for occasional users.

The county warns that someone without a real estate background may do better to visit the office for help locating a document.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. It is at 1926 Hall Ave, Marinette, WI 54143, and the phone number is 715-732-7551. Packages from FedEx or UPS go to 1925 Ella Court.

Does Marinette County accept electronic recording?

Yes. The county lists CSC (866-403-5272) and Simplifile (800-460-5657) as electronic recording providers. Ask whoever is handling your closing whether they will submit the deed through one of them.

Who pays the transfer fee when I sell a house in Marinette County?

The seller, who is called the grantor in the statute. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. Both buyer and seller sign the electronic transfer return.

Are Marinette County records available online?

Yes. LandShark offers documents recorded from 1990 forward, and registering and viewing the index is free. The daily-user option is built for firms that view and buy images. For anything older than 1990, ask the Register of Deeds at 715-732-7551 how to get a copy.
